tells: 1. No laugh builds across the strip: over the full second the faces stay close to neutral, with only small head turns and one hand lift (white top, centre). Nobody's shoulders, chest or head pitch reads as a laugh starting (club-5-strip.png, front table row across all six frames)

2. The front row is a lineup of near-identical poses: forearms flat on the table, hands clasped by the candle, torsos square to camera. It reads as posed figures rather than a listening crowd (club-1-wide.png, front tables, centre to right)

3. The face close shows low-poly geometry: the faceted shoulder and collar on the blonde at left and the polygonal jacket on the man at right. The lead face has waxy, uniform skin and a stiff half-smile with glassy eyes (club-4-face.png, left third and right third; centre face)

4. The green-hoodie man has his face buried under his cap brim and reads as a dead, slumped figure. In the other mid shot he is mid-speech with his mouth open, so the poses are inconsistent (club-6-held.png, centre-left table; club-3-mid.png, centre)

5. The back rows are uniformly lit standing silhouettes that look like flat cut-outs, with no seated weight or motion between frames (club-1-wide.png and club-2-mid.png, upper-middle band under the bar sign)

1. Flat, skin-coloured polygon shards (collapsed low-LOD hands or forearms) float beside the second-row seats and next to bodies, a hard immersion breaker (theatre-4-face.png, left and right of the face at about x 380 and x 1060; theatre-2-mid.png, about x 270, 420 and 770 at y 400; theatre-1-wide.png, about x 600 and 890 at y 450)

2. The second row and the rows behind float or stand far above their seat backs instead of sitting in them, so heads are a full torso too high and the rake looks wrong (theatre-1-wide.png, middle band; theatre-6-held.png, row behind the front row)

3. The front row has identical, rigid seated poses: knees spread, hands on knees, spines bolt upright, shoulders hunched. It looks like a mannequin bench (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-6-held.png, front row)

4. The laugh in the strip is scattered: a few mouths open (the blonde and the man in the jacket) while others look down at their laps or turn away. It reads as random chatter, not a response caused by a line (theatre-5-strip.png, front row, frames 12.6 to 13.0)

5. The house is very dark and flat-lit, with a blue-black haze and almost no rim separation, so the back two-thirds of the frame is a mass of identical dark silhouettes against the bright practicals (theatre-1-wide.png, upper half)

1. The laugh shows as people turning to talk to their neighbour (heads swung sideways, mouths moving) rather than laughing toward the stage. Nobody throws their head back or drops their shoulders, so it reads as conversation, not reaction (openmic-5-strip.png, centre pair in green and black hoodie, frames 12.6 to 13.0)
2. The front row sits in a straight lineup with near-identical hands-on-knees, lean-forward poses, the same pose cloned along the bench (openmic-1-wide.png, front row; openmic-3-mid.png, right half)

3. The hair outline shows stippled, dithered transparency, and a faceted, paddle-like hand floats at the background woman's chest (openmic-4-face.png, right edge of the hair about x 780 to 880; background blonde, hand at about x 1120, y 580)

4. Bodies interpenetrate on the crowded bench: the green-top woman's arm and shoulder sink into the dark-hoodie woman, and the forearms at far right are pale and faceted (openmic-2-mid.png, centre right; openmic-6-held.png, right edge)

5. The same cast appears in every venue (green hoodie, purple top, pink jacket, short blonde, yellow henley), and the back row is a few people standing against a bare wall with a glowing blank panel. The room feels thinly populated and staged (openmic-1-wide.png, back wall and the left panel at about x 220, y 300)
